text: 🇲🇽🌎 On the U.S. border, Sheinbaum drew the line: cooperation, yes — subordination, never. "That's what we aspire to: a good relationship with our neighbor to the north. But cooperation always, subordination never. That is the essence of us Mexicans." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León She recalled the good moments between the two nations — Juárez and Lincoln, Cárdenas and Roosevelt, AMLO and Trump's first term — as the model: cooperation between equals, on Mexico's own terms.

🇲🇽✊ When she reached the presidency, a comedian sneered that "a housewife has arrived." Her reply: "With great pride I am a housewife, a mother, a grandmother — and by the will of the people of Mexico, supreme commander of the armed forces." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León She announced a new pension for women aged 60–64 that recognizes unpaid care work. "Women can be whatever we want to be. There are no limits."

🇲🇽✊ A former president called seniors who receive the pension "a bunch of lazy people." Sheinbaum answered him. "For us, older adults are heroes and heroines of the homeland. They have given their lives to their families, their communities, their state and their country." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León Mexico is the only country where every adult over 65 receives a pension — now written into the Constitution. In Nuevo León alone, 583,000 seniors receive it.

🇲🇽✊ They said raising the minimum wage would bring inflation, kill investment, and crash the peso. The opposite happened. "The minimum wage went up — and there is record foreign direct investment, no inflation, and the peso is one of the strongest currencies in the world." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León In 2018 Mexico's minimum wage was 2,800 pesos a month. Today it is over 9,500 — a 154% increase in real terms.

🇲🇽⚖️ Mexico abolished slavery in 1810 — decades before the United States. "We were the first country on the continent to call for the abolition of slavery. The United States did so much later — and had a Civil War over it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Second Report, Nuevo León Hidalgo proclaimed the end of slavery in 1810, at the very start of the independence war. The U.S. did not abolish it until 1865, after a war that split the country.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico's new-car sales top 1 million in 8 months for the first time ever</u>

Mexicans bought 1,014,832 new light vehicles from January to August 2026 — up 4.7% year-on-year and the first time domestic sales have cleared a million before September, per INEGI/AMIA data reported by El Financiero. August alone moved 129,479 units, the second-strongest August in the industry's history. A home market this strong is the flip side of the peso's best run in two years.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex contained a Salina Cruz refinery flare-up in under 6 minutes, zero injuries</u>

A pinhole in a heater coil (H-201-B) sparked a small fire at the Salina Cruz refinery's Alto Vacío 1 unit in Oaxaca on Sept 4 during a scheduled maintenance shutdown. Pemex controlled it in under six minutes with no injuries and no impact on output — the refinery "continues operating" normally and the incident "did not represent a risk for the installation's operation."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>When crime offers kids more than the state does, that's the alarm — Mexico's CNDH</u>

Mexico's human-rights commission put the root cause plainly: "When a girl, boy or adolescent finds greater opportunities within a criminal structure than in the institutions of the state, there is a warning signal." The CNDH is pressing for prevention through education, sports, culture and jobs, naming poverty, school dropout, family violence and absent state presence — not "bad seeds" — as what feeds recruitment. It's the same atención-a-las-causas logic the 4T built its security strategy on.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The García Luna years: how Washington built Mexico's security state under Calderón</u>

A Contralínea investigation lays out the deepest US penetration of Mexico's security apparatus: the Mérida Initiative, the US-wired "Plataforma México" surveillance grid with 600+ nodes across the country, $2.5M in polygraph gear, and Operation Fast and Furious, which walked guns straight to the Sinaloa Cartel. The centerpiece was García Luna's 7,000 m² command bunker, inaugurated Nov 24, 2009 by US Ambassador Carlos Pascual with Calderón at his side. That same García Luna now sits in a US prison for working for the cartel Washington claimed to be fighting.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>Mexico is doubling its railways — 2,377 km of new passenger and freight track</u>

Sheinbaum's government is laying 2,377 km of new rail — double what the entire previous administration built — with military engineers already about 800 km into four simultaneous corridors: AIFA–Pachuca, CDMX–Querétaro, Querétaro–Irapuato and Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo. Passenger service starts returning between November 2026 and February 2027, on the way to more than 3,000 km by 2030 — reversing decades of neoliberal dismantling of Mexico's trains.
